title: Commercial Energy Consumption Analytics and Anomaly Alerts MVP
description: Deliver the approved MVP capabilities for authorized CSV meter-data ingestion, consumption analysis, rolling baselines, anomaly detection and alerts, peer benchmarking when valid data exists, account-manager ranking, and authorized CSV or PDF exports.

epics.title: FR-1 Meter Reading Data Ingestion
epics.description: Accept and validate authorized CSV meter readings for a selected customer site.

stories.title: As a Meter Data Operations Specialist, I want to upload a valid CSV for a selected customer site so that the site has usable consumption data.
As a Meter Data Operations Specialist, I want clear invalid-file feedback so that I can correct meter data without creating an unusable dataset.

epics.title: FR-2 Consumption Dashboard and Period Aggregation
epics.description: Present accepted site consumption in daily, weekly, and monthly views with explicit data states.

stories.title: As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want to view daily consumption for an authorized site and date range so that I can understand day-to-day usage.
As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want to switch between weekly and monthly consumption views so that I can understand longer-term usage trends.

epics.title: FR-3 Rolling Four-Week Baseline
epics.description: Calculate and display a valid baseline from the 28 calendar days preceding each evaluated day.

stories.title: As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want to see a valid rolling four-week baseline beside daily actual consumption so that I can recognize material deviations.

epics.title: FR-4 Anomaly Detection and Chart Highlighting
epics.description: Detect daily consumption above the active threshold and distinguish flagged days in the chart.

stories.title: As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want days exceeding the approved anomaly threshold to be identified accurately so that I can focus on unusual consumption.
As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want anomaly days to be visually distinguishable on the consumption chart so that I can find them without relying only on color.

epics.title: FR-5 Account Manager Alerts
epics.description: Create authorized anomaly alerts for the account manager assigned to the affected customer.

stories.title: As a Commercial Account Manager, I want to review anomaly alerts for my assigned customers and open the associated site context so that I can prepare follow-up conversations.

epics.title: FR-6 Peer Benchmarking
epics.description: Show a non-identifying peer comparison when valid anonymized comparison data is available.

stories.title: As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want to see an anonymized peer comparison or a benchmark-unavailable state so that I can understand my site's relative consumption without exposing other customers.

epics.title: FR-7 Account Manager Customer Ranking
epics.description: Allow account managers to rank only their assigned customers by anomaly count or deviation severity.

stories.title: As a Commercial Account Manager, I want to rank only my assigned customers by anomaly count or deviation severity so that I can prioritize follow-up work.

epics.title: FR-8 Consumption Report Export
epics.description: Produce authorized consumption reports for a selected date range in CSV or PDF format.

stories.title: As a Commercial Customer Operations Lead, I want to export authorized site consumption data as CSV for a selected date range so that I can use the data in operational analysis.
As a Commercial Account Manager, I want to export an authorized PDF consumption report for an assigned site and date range so that I can support customer conversations.

notes:
Product Backlog: The MVP consists of eight features, one per FR-1 through FR-8, decomposed into twelve INVEST-oriented stories. P0 denotes high delivery priority for the MVP, while P1 denotes an MVP feature that depends on approved peer-data governance. No P2 stories are included because the approved PRD does not define later-scope functionality for this backlog.

Definition of Ready: A story is ready when its PRD traceability is confirmed; its persona, goal, benefit, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and estimate are understood; authorization impacts are identified; and all applicable TBD decisions have been approved or explicitly deferred without blocking the story. Data-dependent stories additionally require representative authorized test data and agreed data-quality rules.

Definition of Done: A story is done when its acceptance criteria pass using representative data; role and assignment authorization boundaries are verified; invalid, no-data, unavailable, progress, and actionable error states required by the PRD are implemented where applicable; telemetry is emitted without raw meter readings or unnecessary personal data; accessible labels, keyboard interactions, and non-color-only indicators are validated where relevant; and the change is validated behind the approved feature-flag rollout approach.
acceptance_criteria: The backlog traces each approved functional requirement FR-1 through FR-8 to one epic and at least one user story.
Every user story defines a persona-based statement, description, priority, release, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and an XS, S, M, or L estimate.
No backlog item introduces direct back-office integration, billing, non-CSV ingestion, equipment control, automated remediation, or external notification functionality.

research.title: Commercial Energy Analytics Product and Business Analysis
research.description: Approved persona, assumption, constraint, risk, and discovery-question context used to refine the backlog without expanding scope.
